about: Closed variety of the driver golden lives here (FR-13): the files recorded, the normalisation rows, the files kept as full text, the tree exclusions, the scenario exclusions, the caps. Read by driver_trace.py and driver_golden.py; nothing at runtime reads it.

known_blind_spots.patch: hooklib.load_ref_json (module attribute replaced by a lambda)
known_blind_spots.effect: the call is absorbed: no fake_call, and no I/O of its own; seen only if a move makes the patch stop intercepting (the real read then shows as a different trace)

known_blind_spots.patch: execution_request.fresh_evidence (module attribute replaced, restored on exit)
known_blind_spots.where: story_run_common.py (the evidence fake, line ~494) used by the stand and S6 files

known_blind_spots.effect: as above; the controller class the driver builds is a stand-in
the recorder's own Popen wrapper is the patched object: a spawn seen through the spy is not recorded as a spawn; the scenario's own assertions are the guard

path_rows: N1 the plugin root -> <PLUGIN>; N2 sys.executable -> <PY>; N3 each registered temp root -> <ROOT-n> (numbered by first registration in the scenario); N4 the temp dir -> <TMP>. Every spelling (str, resolve, realpath, 8.3 short, forward slashes, JSON double backslashes), the drive letter case-insensitive; a longer match wins, so a path under <PLUGIN> and <TMP> is <PLUGIN>. Code: driver_trace.Registry.

rows.scope: any text: an ISO-8601 date-time; a date alone is kept

JSON key duration_ms, created_at, stage_started, stage_finished, wall_seconds: a number (the controller's epoch floats and measured seconds); a null is kept, so a stage with no end time is still different from one with
path: driver-tmp/<op>-<ten or more digits>.json (story_run.controller)
path: <name>.<32 hex>.tmp (event_store.atomic_json)
path: recovery-<32 hex>.bin
JSON key event_id (event_store; the activity spans carry <32 hex>:start and <32 hex>:end - the suffix is kept)
every later occurrence of a token N8/N9a registered; a 32-hex value never registered is kept
JSON key source_revision: the sha of the ticket snapshot -> <REV=snapshot>, any other 64 hex -> <REV-n>
loopback host:port
an object repr's address
traceback line of the driver; a story_step.py frame is kept
story_progress's clock time of the progress line ('since 21:15', 'the scout started 01:05')
the elapsed time that follows it ('(0 min)', '(3 h 12 min)', '(2 days)')
JSON key event_hash, previous_hash (event_store: a hash over the event's own event_id and created_at); the events themselves are compared as the full text of state/events.jsonl in the tree records

JSON key input_hash, and hash inside a source_manifest (the dashboard/metrics refresh: a hash over files whose text holds a temp path). Q13: the hashed content itself is compared elsewhere - pipeline.json and state/events.jsonl as full text, every other state file by its normalised sha in the tree records; only the hash's own agreement is hidden

JSON key question_sha (driver-answers.jsonl: question_body_sha over a body that holds the project's temp path). Q13: the question's text is compared in full in driver-question.md / driver-questions.jsonl / driver-question.answered.md (kept as text); only the hash's agreement is hidden
the dashboard's feedback age ('age days: 0.06'): an elapsed time, rendered from the same age_days / age_weeks N6 hides in the JSON
git log's default Date line of a commit the rig just made

a LINE that starts with one git commit id and ends there or goes on after a tab (`git rev-parse HEAD`, `for-each-ref --format=%(objectname)`, `ls-remote`, `log --format=%H%x09%s` of a throwaway repo the rig builds: the id depends on the commit's date). Anchored to the line; the repository's own files and commit messages are compared elsewhere, only the id is hidden
every later occurrence of an id N28a registered; a 40-hex value never registered is kept
a 12-hex abbreviation (the driver's short form) of an id N28a registered; a 12-hex value that starts no registered id is kept

path: telemetry/command-<pid>.jsonl and hook-<pid>.jsonl (the telemetry file is named by the writing process's id): <PID-proc> when the id is a process this scenario spawned (or the test process itself), else <PID>; BEYOND: another prefix or nine digits are kept
path: <name>.<pid>.tmp (host_receipt's atomic write names its temp file by the process id): <PID-proc> or <PID> as N27; BEYOND: nine or more digits are kept

brief_pack's own stdout line `brief: <path> (2,585 B)` and the driver's relay of it with `note: ` in front: the size of a brief whose text holds the project's own path, so it moves with the directory's length (t-374, found by recording one package in two directories). The brief's text is compared through the sha of the file brief_pack wrote; only the printed size is hidden

every value of the key package_fingerprint (runtime_paths.resolve_runtime: a sha over EVERY non-test file of the package, story_run.py and any driver_* module included) in controller.json, events.jsonl and the controller's tmp packets, also inside an escaped JSON string. It changes with every package byte, so it would make every move look like a difference; the package's own files are compared by K14, not by this value (t-372 F1). BEYOND: another 64-hex under another key is kept

the `bytes` of a driver-questions.jsonl row: the length of the question text, which holds the project's own path, so it moves with the length of the directory (t-372 F2: a relocated package with the same bytes). The question's text itself is compared in full (driver-question.md, driver-questions.jsonl's neighbours); only its length is hidden
a file whose WHOLE text is an epoch time (telemetry/.rotated-at); anchored, so a number inside any other text is untouched

JSON key fingerprint, 16 hex (integrations/tracker-write.json: tracker_write.fingerprint, a hash of the channel's settings, which vary per temp project). Q13: the file's other fields are compared in the same record; only the fingerprint's agreement is hidden

JSON key pid (state.in_flight, B-268: the claude process's id, an OS number): <PID-proc> for a process of this scenario - so the driver's OWN pid written where a child's belongs is visible (t-372 F7) - else <PID>

JSON key packet_hash (the controller's packet: a hash over a packet that holds the project's temp path). Q13: the packet's own fields are compared in the same record's text; only the hash's agreement is hidden
a date, a time and the word UTC in a sentence ('as when the person answered at 2026-10-02 23:02 UTC'); N5 needs the T
the dashboard's 'Generated <date> <hh:mm>' line (no T, so N5 does not see it)

a temp dir of an EARLIER scenario of the same process left in os.environ by the rig's driver_for (STORY_RUN_CLAUDE, STUB_CONTROL, STUB_LOG): not registered by this scenario, its name is random. The rig's process-wide environment write is a noted analog (t-301 N0 handoff)

ambient_scrub_reason: Variables the DRIVER itself puts into every environment it builds (so env_delta shows them as set by the code) but that a host shell may already carry: the Bash tool lacks GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, the PowerShell tool has it, so the same code showed a delta in one shell and none in the other. The test process is started without them, whatever the ambient holds. Any other name a shell adds and the driver also sets needs a row here.
